proof: Write the 1999 terms as u_k=a+kd for 0<=k<=1998. If two terms are integers, then d is rational; write d=p/q in lowest terms. The integer terms then occur in one residue class of indices modulo q, so their number is either floor(1999/q) or ceil(1999/q). Conversely, either count can be realized by choosing d=1/q and shifting a to place the selected residue class at the long or short position. For q=28, 1999/q is between 71 and 72, while for q=29 it is between 68 and 69. Hence 70 is impossible. The values for q=29,30,31,32 yield the adjacent pairs {68,69}, {66,67}, {64,65}, and {62,63}. For every q>=32, consecutive values 1999/q and 1999/(q+1) differ by less than 2, so the adjacent floor/ceiling pairs cannot skip an integer. As q runs onward to 1999, these pairs therefore cover every integer from 1 through 69. Thus every positive count below 70 is attainable and the smallest impossible count is 70.
spu_outline: Represent the progression by a+kd.
Show two integer terms force a rational common difference.
Characterize integer indices as one residue class modulo q.
Derive the floor/ceiling count formula and its converse.
Exclude 70 using q=28 and q=29.
Show the adjacent floor/ceiling bands cover 1 through 69.

candidate_answer: f(n)=g(n) for every positive integer n
proof: The identities imply by induction that f(g^k(n))=f(n)+k and g(f^k(n))=g(n)+k. They also imply that f and g have exactly the same fibers: f(a)=f(b) gives g(a)=g(b) after applying g to both equal values and using g(f(x))=g(x)+1, and the reverse follows symmetrically. This yields a well-defined bijection T from im(f) to im(g) with T(f(n))=g(n). Moreover both images are upward closed, because f(g(n))=f(n)+1 and g(f(n))=g(n)+1. I did not close the remaining step proving that this induced bijection T is the identity on the two image tails; asserting monotonicity or injectivity of f or g here would be unjustified.
unresolved_gap: Prove from the two conjugacy-type identities on the image tails that T(x)=x, without assuming monotonicity or injectivity of f and g.

Prove equality of the fiber partitions of f and g.
Define the induced bijection between their images.
Show both images are upward closed.

proof: Because t^(1/3) is concave on the positive reals, Jensen gives S <= 3*cuberoot(((a^2+2bc)+(b^2+2ca)+(c^2+2ab))/3). The numerator is (a+b+c)^2=36, so S<=3*cuberoot(12). Equality is attained at a=b=c=2. Equality in Jensen requires the three radicands to be equal. Their pairwise differences are (a-b)(a+b-2c), (b-c)(b+c-2a), and (c-a)(c+a-2b); for positive a,b,c with sum 6, the simultaneous equalities force a=b=c. Hence the maximum is 3*cuberoot(12).

Insert the sum constraint.

candidate_answer: Real solutions exist exactly for |a|>=2 and are x=(a±sqrt(a^2-4))/2, with the two signs coinciding when |a|=2.
proof: Let A=1+x+x^2. For real x, A=(x+1/2)^2+3/4>0, and 1+x^2+x^4=A^2-2xA. Substitution into the equation gives (a-1)A^2=(a+1)(A^2-2xA). Dividing by 2A is legal and reduces the equation to A=(a+1)x, equivalently x^2-ax+1=0. Therefore the real solutions are x=(a±sqrt(a^2-4))/2 when a^2>=4, and there are no real solutions when |a|<2. The exceptional values a=±1 require no separate recovery because A>0 made the reduction equivalent; the quadratic gives no real root for them.

Rewrite 1+x^2+x^4 as A^2-2xA.
Reduce equivalently to x^2-ax+1=0.
Classify by the discriminant.

candidate_answer: (a) 1<=a_1<=2. (b) Yes, a_2020=a_1 for every allowed starting value.
proof: For t=2, let T(x)=(x+2)/(x+1). On x>0 this map is decreasing. It maps [4/3,3/2] into [T(3/2),T(4/3)]=[7/5,10/7], which is contained in [4/3,3/2]. Thus all a_n for n>=2 lie in the required interval exactly when a_2=T(a_1) does. Solving 4/3<=(a_1+2)/(a_1+1)<=3/2 with a_1>0 gives 1<=a_1<=2. For t=-3, T(x)=(x-3)/(x+1). Direct calculation gives T^2(x)=-(x+3)/(x-1) and T^3(x)=x wherever the iterates are defined. The only starting values that cause a forbidden denominator in the first two steps are -1 and 1, precisely the excluded values. Since a_2020=T^2019(a_1) and 2019 is divisible by 3, a_2020=a_1.

Prove the target interval is invariant.
Solve the condition on a_2 for a_1.
